record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: Over what range of temporal and spatial scales is Taylor's hypothesis valid for kinetic plasma turbulence? The open issue is whether the usual conversion between temporal spacecraft measurements and spatial structure remains reliable across the broad range of scales relevant to kinetic turbulence.

evidence.quote: This includes answering fundamental questions about, for instance, ... (iv) the validity of Taylor’s hypothesis over a broad range of time and spatial scales.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a magnetized, weakly collisional plasma exhibiting kinetic turbulence (e.g., a stellar/solar wind) advected past a stationary probe with bulk flow velocity $\mathbf{U}_0$. Taylor's hypothesis is the assumption that temporal fluctuations $\delta f(t)$ measured by the stationary probe at a fixed spatial point are dominated by the rigid advection of spatial structures past the probe, so that an observed angular frequency $\omega_{\rm sc}$ is related to a wavevector $\mathbf{k}$ in the plasma frame by $\omega_{\rm sc} = \mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{U}_0$, allowing the conversion of time series into spatial spectra via $k = \omega_{\rm sc}/U_0$.

Let $L$ denote the energy-containing (outer) scale of the turbulence, $\rho_i$ the ion gyroradius, $d_i = c/\omega_{pi}$ the ion inertial length, $\rho_e$ the electron gyroradius, and let $V_A$ be the Alfvén speed and $\delta V$ the rms turbulent velocity fluctuation amplitude at scale $\ell$. In the magnetohydrodynamic inertial range ($\ell \gg \rho_i$), the standard sufficient condition $\delta V \ll U_0$ (and, when relevant, $V_A \ll U_0$, i.e., super-Alfvénic flow) is known to render Taylor's hypothesis reliable. At sub-ion (kinetic) scales ($\ell \lesssim \rho_i$), however, dispersive wave modes (e.g., kinetic Alfvén waves, whistlers) can have intrinsic frequencies $\omega(\mathbf{k})$ comparable to or exceeding $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{U}_0$, potentially violating the hypothesis.

Determine the precise range of temporal frequencies $\omega_{\rm sc}$ and spatial scales $\ell$ (spanning from $L$ down through $\rho_i$, $d_i$, and into the sub-electron scales $\ell \lesssim \rho_e$) over which Taylor's hypothesis $\omega_{\rm sc} = \mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{U}_0$ remains a quantitatively reliable conversion between single-point temporal measurements and spatial structure for fully developed three-dimensional kinetic plasma turbulence. Equivalently, characterize, in terms of the dimensionless parameters $\delta V/U_0$, $V_A/U_0$, $k\rho_i$, $k d_i$, $k\rho_e$, and the angle between $\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{U}_0$, the regime in which the hypothesis holds and the regime in which it fails.
artifact.status_search_result: Several studies have analyzed the validity of Taylor's hypothesis at kinetic scales: Howes et al. (2014, arXiv:1405.5460) showed it holds for kinetic Alfvén waves but can fail for whistler-supported dissipation ranges; subsequent works (Chhiber et al. 2019; Bourouaine & Perez 2018; Perez et al. 2021 for Parker Solar Probe; Zank et al. 2022 for the heliosheath) refined the conditions in terms of $\delta V/(V_A+U_0)$, dispersion, and obliquity. A complete, scale-resolved characterization spanning the full MHD-to-sub-electron range remains an active research problem with no single closed-form answer, so the question is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Validity of the Taylor Hypothesis for Linear Kinetic Waves in the Weakly Collisional Solar Wind
status_evidence.snippet: A dissipation range supported by whistler waves is likely to violate the Taylor hypothesis, while one supported by kinetic Alfven waves is not.
status_evidence.claim: Validity depends on the dispersive wave mode populating the kinetic range.

status_evidence.title: Applicability of Taylor's hypothesis during Parker Solar Probe perihelia
status_evidence.snippet: Modified Taylor's hypothesis valid when delta V/(V_A+U_0) is sufficiently small.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative criteria continue to be refined for sub-Alfvenic and trans-Alfvenic flows.

status_evidence.title: On the applicability of Taylor's hypothesis in streaming MHD turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Taylor's hypothesis is applicable to magnetic turbulence only when turbulent velocity fluctuations can be neglected against the bulk flow speed.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions established in MHD inertial range; kinetic-range conditions remain under study.
